open_ports.version: Net-SNMP (version unconfirmed; community strings not yet tested)

cve_candidates.description: Memcached 1.5.5 and earlier exposed on UDP port 11211 allows unauthenticated UDP amplification attacks (DDoS reflection factor up to 51,000x). Also enables unauthenticated read/write of all cached keys, potentially exposing session tokens, credentials, and application secrets stored in cache.

Unauthenticated access to Memcached allows attackers to flush, read, and overwrite cache entries. In web application contexts this can lead to session hijacking, privilege escalation, or poisoning of application logic.
Net-SNMP through 5.9.3 has a NULL pointer dereference in handler.c via crafted SNMP packets, causing a daemon crash (DoS). Requires access to the SNMP port with any community string.
Net-SNMP through 5.9.3 has a NULL pointer dereference in handler.c that can be triggered remotely via SNMP SET requests on certain OIDs.

SNMP community string brute force via default strings (public/private/community). Successful community string enumeration allows SNMP walk to retrieve running processes, installed software, network interfaces, routing tables, and potentially credentials stored in OIDs.

rpcbomb: rpcbind before 0.2.4, LIBTIRPC before 1.0.1 and 1.0.2-rc before 1.0.2-rc3, and NTIRPC before 1.4.3 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-memory and crash) via a large number of requests.

NFS exports with no_root_squash or misconfigured export options allow a remote attacker to mount the share and write files as root. If /etc/exports contains world-readable or no_root_squash entries, an attacker can plant SSH authorized_keys or SUID binaries for privilege escalation.
OpenVPN 2.5.1 and earlier allows authentication bypass via deferred authentication plugins when the --auth-user-pass-verify or similar plugin is used, potentially allowing unauthenticated VPN access.

attack_surface_summary: The target host 172.19.0.2 (redteam_easy-target-1.redteam_easy_engagement-net) presents a unique attack surface: all 65,535 TCP ports are actively closed (TCP RST), but UDP scanning reveals 8 services in open|filtered states across ports 67 (DHCP), 111 (rpcbind/ONC-RPC), 138 (NetBIOS-DGM), 161 (SNMP), 1194 (OpenVPN), 2049 (NFS), 11211 (Memcached), and 27017 (likely MongoDB). This profile is consistent with a containerised HTB target intentionally exposing only UDP-based infrastructure services. The highest-priority initial access vectors are: (1) SNMP on 161/udp — default community strings (public/private) should be brute-forced immediately; a successful SNMP walk can reveal running processes, installed packages, network topology, user accounts, and potentially credentials; (2) NFS on 2049/udp + rpcbind on 111/udp — showmount enumeration may reveal world-readable or no_root_squash exports enabling direct filesystem access or SUID binary planting; (3) Memcached on 11211/udp — entirely unauthenticated, allowing full cache dump which may contain session tokens, API keys, or application credentials; (4) MongoDB on 27017/udp — if accessible without authentication (a common misconfiguration), it exposes all database contents. The NetBIOS-DGM (138/udp) and DHCP (67/udp) presence suggests a Windows-adjacent or Samba environment, warranting SMB credential spray attempts. The OpenVPN service on 1194/udp may be a pivot point into an internal network segment. Privilege escalation paths likely run through NFS root squash bypass (write SSH keys or SUID binaries to exported shares) or through credentials harvested via SNMP/Memcached being reused on management interfaces not yet discovered. The complete absence of TCP services is atypical and may indicate a secondary access mechanism (port knocking, VPN-gated services) that becomes available post-initial-foothold.
